bug_semantics: Stored XSS (CWE-79) in rich-text @-mention rendering. parseMention in web-frontend/modules/core/editor/mention.js builds a raw HTML span with a template literal that interpolates workspace user.name into both the data-label attribute and the element body with no encoding. A display name containing a double quote closes that attribute and the opening tag, so following markup becomes live DOM. PATCH /api/user/account/ stores first_name verbatim (AccountSerializer, no HTML sanitization). markdown.js registers parseMention, and grid/card rich-text components (GridViewFieldRichText.vue, FunctionalGridViewFieldRichText.vue, RowCardFieldRichText.vue) render the result through v-html, so any workspace member who views a cell that mentions the attacker executes the payload without a click. The payload lives in the account name until the name or mentioning row is removed. First released in 1.24.0; still unescaped at 2.2.2; 2.3.0 escapes before interpolation.
flaw_origin: GitLab MR !2200 / issue #2041 added mentions to long-text fields. Commit a41ab1ac87009d87db9a06c8a6973b8df954c26d created mention.js and first wrote parseMention's unescaped return `@${user.name}`, then wired it through parseMarkdown. Immediate parent 976bccde3b2722d3a392fd0361a3f87789d90ab6 has no mention.js and no data-label interpolation; editor mentions used TipTap structured renderHTML arrays, not HTML strings. 8636a082 later only moved the className block inside if (user) and left the interpolation intact until a870dc0d added escapeHtml.
